result.topic_en: A worked numerical example finding all complex roots of the trinomial equation x^7 - 3x^2 + 2 = 0 (and of its derivative) in polar form using logarithms, followed by the general equations that determine the argument R of a root of a trinomial equation with complex coefficients.

methods.what: Numerical determination of all complex roots of the trinomial x^7 - 3x^2 + 2 = 0 in polar form (log modulus and argument) via logarithmic computation of angles theta, 2theta, 5theta, 7theta
Constant 3^7/2^5 used in the trinomial root computation
Roots of the derivative equation 7x^6 - 6x = 0 computed (0 and the fifth roots of 6/7) and corresponding values
methods.quote: Die sechs Wurzeln der derivirten Gleichung sind

methods.what: For a trinomial with complex coefficients, the argument R of a root satisfies proportionality of sines to a r^alpha, b r^beta, c r^gamma
methods.quote: $\frac{\sin(\gamma-\beta)R + C - B}{ar^\alpha} = \frac{\sin(\alpha-\gamma)R + A - C}{br^\beta} = \frac{\sin(\beta-\alpha)R + B - A}{cr^\gamma}$

methods.what: Equation eliminating r to determine R for complex-coefficient trinomial
methods.quote: $a^{\gamma-\beta} b^{\alpha-\gamma} c^{\beta-\alpha} = (\sin((\gamma-\beta)R + C - B))^{\gamma-\beta} . \sin((\alpha-\gamma)R + A - C)^{\alpha-\gamma} . \sin((\beta-\alpha)R + B - A)^{\beta-\alpha}$
